items.body_excerpt:
Presented By
NRL Late Mail: Round 25 - Teddy out again
Roosters fullback James Tedesco will miss a third straight game due to an ankle injury after being unable to recover in time to face Wests Tigers on Sunday.
Roosters coach Trent Robinson told media after training on Saturday it had been frustrating recovery for the No.1.
"It's been, obviously, a bit frustrating for Ted and we've named him each week, but he's not right to play this week," he said.
"He's progressed quite well, but it's a bit more niggly than what we thought."
Robinson said the plan was to attempt to build his training load to work towards a return in their Round 26 top-four clash with the Dolphins.

NRL Casualty Ward: Koula injures ankle; Tedesco still hobbled
Manly speedster Tolu Koula has suffered a syndesmosis injury after he was on the end of a hip drop tackle from Dom Young on Saturday.
Koula was dragged down just short of the tryline by the Knights winger but was unable to get back to his feet.
Young was sent to the sin bin and Koula was ruled out of the rest of the match.
In Saturday's late game between the Dragons and the Bulldogs, St George Illawarra hooker Jacob Liddle was ruled out early in the first half with a calf injury.
"The medical staff have just told me that they think he's tore his calf, so it's not his Achilles, so fingers crossed, that's where it lands," coach Dean Young said after the game.
Before kick off, Bulldogs back Enari Tuala was a late scratching with a knee injury.
Bulldogs utility Kurt Mann later joined him on the sidelines with a groin injury.
“It looks like just a one-week thing, he just aggravated something at training on Thursday night," coach Cameron Ciraldo said post-match.
“Kurt, bit unfortunate there that he sort of got injured straight away when he came on …
“It doesn't look like he'll be right next week, but hopefully it's not too long."
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
Sunia Turuva was initially named on the six-man bench but dropped out of the squad in Saturday's 24-hour update as he battles a knee injury suffered last weekend.
In positive news, Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
The Roosters have again ruled skipper James Tedesco out late in the week as he continues to battle an ankle injury.
Tedesco has already missed two games and won't line up against Wests Tigers.
"It's been, obviously, a bit frustrating for Ted and we've named him each week, but he's not right to play this week," said coach Trent Robinson.
"He's progressed quite well, but it's a bit more niggly than what we thought."
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh has had surgery on his ankle and is facing an eight-week recovery time.
Walsh had scans on Sunday which confirmed he had sustained a high-grade syndesmosis injury during the loss to the Warriors on Saturday night.
Warriors fullback Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad has subsequently been banned for two games for a hip drop tackle.
With Australia's World Cup opener against the Kiwis set down for Thursday, October 15 it appears Walsh's chances of representing the Kangaroos are gone.
The Raiders had Simi Sasagi back from a shoulder injury for their clash with the Broncos but lost back-rower Zac Hosking to a hamstring injury during the second half.

NRL Round 25 closes at Allianz Stadium with the biggest mismatch on the card, as the first placed Roosters take on a Wests Tigers side sitting near the bottom of the competition. The market agrees, installing Sydney as a massive 22.5-point favourite, and while spreads this large always bring diminishing returns, I am still prepared to lay the number.
The Roosters moved to the top of the ladder with a superb 12-6 win over Penrith last week and are chasing a ninth consecutive victory. James Tedesco returns after two matches out with an ankle injury, giving the competition leaders another major boost as they push toward the minor premiership. Wests, meanwhile, lost another close game 24-22 to the Dragons and now lose Adam Doueihi for the remainder of the season due to shoulder surgery. Jock Madden returns at halfback.
This is not the type of spread I want to attack with a huge stake. Once you get beyond three converted tries, a late consolation score or a favourite easing off can destroy a bet that has otherwise been correct for 75 minutes.
Still, the gap between these teams is enormous. Sydney have won 18 of their past 20 meetings with Wests, and the Tigers are facing the hottest team in the competition.

Sydney’s 12-6 victory over Penrith was arguably their most impressive win of the season. The Roosters did not need a high scoring attacking performance; instead, they rediscovered the “Bondi Wall” and held the Panthers to a single try in a genuine finals contest.
Daly Cherry-Evans was outstanding, scoring both Roosters tries and controlling the match with the composure Sydney recruited him to provide. The veteran produced one of his best performances of the season in what was also another milestone appearance, while the Roosters absorbed prolonged periods of Penrith pressure without cracking.
The result pushed Sydney above Penrith and into first place, extending their winning streak to eight. Now they get Tedesco back.
Cody Ramsey has done an excellent job at fullback, but Tedesco remains the central figure in Sydney’s yardage and support play. His return gives the Roosters another layer of attacking threat around Cherry-Evans and Sam Walker, while Reece Robson continues to provide ruck control from hooker.
The forward rotation also looks capable of overwhelming Wests. Naufahu Whyte and Spencer Leniu start up front, Victor Radley locks the scrum, and Lindsay Collins comes from the bench alongside Connor Watson and the Butcher brothers.

Wests Tigers NRL Injury Report Round 25
Wests Tigers half-back Adam Doueihi will undergo shoulder surgery this week, bringing an end to his 2026 season.
Doueihi suffered the injury in scoring a try against the Cronulla-Sutherland Sharks in Round 9, resulting in the playmaker being out for two months.
The 28-year-old has bravely played on with the injury since returning in Round 17.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers Head of High Performance, Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Wests Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension, he is expected to be out for 1-2 weeks.

There are three rounds remaining in the 2026 NRL regular season and wobbling heavyweights Penrith and Cronulla will be desperate to recover from back-to-back losses this weekend against out-of-contention opposition.
Manly and Canterbury face must-win assignments, while South Sydney has a huge obstacle in front of them in the form of the Warriors.

The finals ship has all but sailed for Melbourne, but knocking over stumbling Penrith in their last home game of the season will provide ample motivation.
FORM: The Storm snapped a three-game losing run to trounce the Sea Eagles 42-20 in Perth in Round 23, after trailing at halftime. They had the bye last weekend.
The Panthers lost their grip on top spot courtesy of a 12-6 loss to the Roosters – their fifth loss in eight games.
INS AND OUTS: Melbourne gets a further boost with Harry Grant and Jack Howarth returning, which sees Tyran Wishart and Joe Chan revert to the bench. Trent Toelau will partner Cam Munster in the halves this week.
Casey McLean is a back in a timely lift for the Panthers, with Paul Alamoti (hamstring) ruled out.
KEY MATCH-UP: Different jersey numbers, but Origin adversaries and Test teammates Munster and Nathan Cleary will guide their teams’ fortunes.
HISTORY: The Storm have won four of their last six against the Panthers but crashed to a 50-10 loss at CommBank Stadium in Round 5.
KEY STAT: The Panthers have a 1-9 record at AAMI Park.
VERDICT: The two biggest heavyweights of the 2020s renew a fierce rivalry, though at a very different juncture than the out-of-contention Storm are used to. But the injury-ravaged side has been gallant in recent defeats and the win over Manly was well-deserved reward.
There’s plenty at stake for the Panthers, who could drop out of the top two with a loss and need to recover some momentum over the closing three rounds.
The Storm are a tempting option with a 7.5-point start after winning five of their last six at home, but the over appeals more with seven of 10 games at AAMI Park producing 52-plus points this season.
